title: Resilient Networking Hub - Building Resilient Ethereum
description:
Ethereum’s resilience is a collective achievement, sustained by protocol researchers, consensus client teams, security practitioners, networking maintainers, and the open-source communities that steward its critical infrastructure. This combined session at the Resilient Networking Hub, within the libp2p Expedition at Devcon 8, brings these perspectives together to explore how we can strengthen the foundations of Ethereum’s resilience.

We will examine libp2p as a shared networking substrate across Ethereum consensus clients, exploring interoperability, implementation diversity, and the challenges of maintaining secure, privacy preserving and permissionless connectivity under adversarial and unreliable network conditions. We will bring a post-quantum perspective to Ethereum’s P2P stack, examining cryptographic exposure in peer identities, discovery handshakes, and transport security, alongside migration strategies including hybrid ML-KEM key exchange, quantum-resistant identity schemes.
abstract: How can we build permissionless networks that survive disconnection, resist censorship, protect privacy, and remain secure against emerging threats? At the Resilient Networking Hub within the libp2p Expedition at Devcon 8, this session brings together Ethereum protocol researchers, networking maintainers, security practitioners, and formal verification contributors to strengthen trust in Ethereum’s underlying infrastructure. We will explore libp2p as a shared networking substrate across Ethereum consensus clients, post-quantum security initiatives by libp2p maintainers, including hybrid ML-KEM key exchange and quantum-resistant peer identities, and privacy-preserving observability to measure network health and identify systemic risks without compromising credible neutrality. We will also examine formal verification through the work of invisible.garden, whose team behind etheorem is building the first consensus implementation in Lean 4, connecting mechanically checked correctness with protocol security, interoperability, and evidence-based risk management. Together, we will identify practical research and engineering opportunities to make Ethereum’s networking infrastructure more resilient, observable, verifiable, and sustainably maintained.
